question: Explain why a capacitor can store charge even though its two plates have equal and opposite charges. Give reason using the concept of potential difference.

options.A: A capacitor cannot store charge because the total charge on its two plates is zero
options.B: Both plates must carry charges of the same sign for a capacitor to store charge
options.C: A capacitor stores charge only when its total charge is non-zero
options.D: Although total charge is zero, equal and opposite charges $+Q$ and $-Q$ remain separated on the plates, creating a potential difference with $Q=CV$
